content.value_statement: Quantum models require careful solver choices and clear analysis workflows. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through QuTiP simulations, measurements, and visualizations.
actual_capabilities: Explains how to create QuTiP quantum states, operators, density matrices, and tensor products.
Guides solver selection for sesolve, mesolve, mcsolve, brmesolve, and Floquet workflows.
Provides examples for expectation values, entropy, fidelity, concurrence, correlations, and steady states.
Shows visualization patterns for Bloch spheres, Wigner functions, Q-functions, histograms, and matrix plots.
Covers advanced topics such as HEOM, stochastic solvers, superoperators, and performance tuning.
limitations: Does not install QuTiP or run simulations unless the user asks the agent to execute code.
Does not validate physical model assumptions or guarantee numerical convergence.
Requires Python, NumPy, Matplotlib, and QuTiP knowledge for complex customization.
Large Hilbert spaces may require separate performance planning and hardware constraints.

use_cases.title: Model Open Quantum Systems
use_cases.description: Set up Hamiltonians, collapse operators, and solvers for dissipative quantum dynamics.

use_cases.title: Teach Quantum Concepts
use_cases.description: Create clear examples for states, operators, measurements, Bloch spheres, and phase-space plots.

use_cases.title: Debug QuTiP Workflows
use_cases.description: Review solver choices, convergence checks, memory use, and plotting steps for a simulation.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Basic Simulation
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the qutip skill to outline a simple two-level quantum system simulation. Include the state, Hamiltonian, solver choice, observables, and plot plan.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Solver
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the qutip skill to compare sesolve, mesolve, and mcsolve for my system. Explain which solver fits my state, dissipation, and measurement needs.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze Entanglement
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the qutip skill to design an analysis plan for two-qubit entanglement decay. Include concurrence, fidelity, collapse operators, and convergence checks.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize a Large Model
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the qutip skill to review my slow open-system simulation. Recommend Hilbert space truncation, stored outputs, tolerance settings, and alternative solvers.

output_examples.input: I need to simulate photon loss in a cavity state.
output_examples.output: The skill would recommend an open-system model, a number operator observable, a photon loss collapse operator, mesolve, and convergence checks.

output_examples.input: I want a visual explanation of a qubit state.
output_examples.output: The skill would guide Bloch sphere setup, state preparation, axis labels, and a clear interpretation of the plotted vector.

output_examples.input: My QuTiP simulation uses too much memory.
output_examples.output: The skill would suggest reducing Hilbert space size, storing selected observables, checking convergence, and reviewing solver options.

best_practices: State the physical system, dimensions, Hamiltonian, initial state, and units before asking for code.
Ask for solver justification when dissipation, mixed states, or stochastic trajectories are involved.
Check convergence by varying Hilbert space size, time steps, tolerances, and trajectory counts.
anti_patterns: Do not assume a small Hilbert space captures all relevant dynamics.
Do not compare solver outputs without matching observables and initial states.
Do not treat example parameters as validated values for a real experiment.

faq.question: What is this skill for?
faq.answer: It helps agents use QuTiP for quantum states, operators, dynamics, analysis, and visualization.

faq.question: Does it run simulations automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples unless the user asks the agent to execute code.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Can it help with open quantum systems?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers collapse operators, master equations, Monte Carlo trajectories, and non-Markovian methods.

faq.question: Can it verify my physics model?
faq.answer: It can review structure and solver choices, but domain validation remains the user responsibility.

faq.question: What should I provide in prompts?
faq.answer: Provide the Hamiltonian, state dimensions, initial state, dissipation terms, observables, and target analysis.
